about: The words of the Backtest Blocks strategy language. Functions, series, calendar and position values go in conditions; settings are "key: value" lines; words are the rest of the rule language. A parameter or definition name is letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore, and is not one of "reserved".

functions.name: sma
functions.summary: simple average of the last n closes
functions.text: Simple average of the last n closes. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in sma(volume, 20).

functions.name: ema
functions.text: Exponential average, started from the simple average of the first n values. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in ema(volume, 20).

functions.name: rsi
functions.text: Relative strength index, from 0 to 100, with Wilder’s smoothing. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in rsi(volume, 14).

functions.name: roc
functions.summary: change over n bars, as a fraction
functions.text: Change over n bars, as a fraction, so compare it with a percentage: roc(20) > 5%. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in roc(volume, 20).

functions.name: stdev
functions.summary: standard deviation of the last n closes
functions.text: Standard deviation of the last n closes, dividing by n. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in stdev(volume, 20).

functions.name: highest
functions.summary: highest high of the last n bars; add [1] to leave out this bar
functions.text: Highest high of the last n bars, this bar included; add [1] to leave out this bar. Without a series it reads high; write another first, as in highest(volume, 20).

functions.name: lowest
functions.summary: lowest low of the last n bars
functions.text: Lowest low of the last n bars, this bar included. Without a series it reads low; write another first, as in lowest(volume, 20).

functions.name: atr
functions.text: Average true range, with Wilder’s smoothing. It takes no series.

functions.name: macd
functions.text: The fast exponential average minus the slow one. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in macd(volume, 12, 26).

functions.name: macd_signal
functions.text: Exponential average of the macd line over signal bars. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in macd_signal(volume, 12, 26, 9).
functions.example: buy when macd() crosses above macd_signal()

functions.name: bb_upper
functions.text: Upper Bollinger band: the average plus width standard deviations. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in bb_upper(volume, 20, 2).

functions.name: bb_lower
functions.text: Lower Bollinger band: the average minus width standard deviations. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in bb_lower(volume, 20, 2).

functions.name: stoch_k
functions.text: Stochastic %K, from 0 to 100: where the close sits between the lowest low and the highest high of the last n bars, averaged over smooth bars (1 for no averaging). It takes no series.

functions.name: stoch_d
functions.summary: stochastic %D: stoch_k averaged over d bars
functions.text: Stochastic %D: stoch_k, with the same n and smooth, averaged over d more bars. It takes no series.
functions.example: buy when stoch_k() crosses above stoch_d()

functions.name: adx
functions.text: Wilder’s average directional index, from 0 to 100: how strong the trend is, whichever way, as the n-bar Wilder average of 100 * |plus_di - minus_di| / (plus_di + minus_di). It takes no series.
functions.example: buy when adx(14) > 25 and plus_di(14) > minus_di(14)

functions.name: plus_di
functions.text: Wilder’s plus directional indicator, from 0 to 100: the Wilder average over n bars of upward movement, divided by that of the true range, times 100. It takes no series.

functions.name: minus_di
functions.text: Wilder’s minus directional indicator, from 0 to 100: the Wilder average over n bars of downward movement, divided by that of the true range, times 100. It takes no series.

functions.name: cci
functions.summary: commodity channel index of the typical price
functions.text: Commodity channel index: the typical price (high + low + close) / 3 minus its n-bar average, divided by 0.015 times its mean absolute deviation from that average. It takes no series.

functions.name: williams_r
functions.text: Williams %R, from -100 to 0: -100 * (highest high - close) / (highest high - lowest low) over the last n bars. It takes no series.

functions.name: mfi
functions.text: Money flow index, from 0 to 100: 100 - 100 / (1 + money flowing in / money flowing out) over the last n bars, where a bar’s flow is its typical price times its volume, counted in when the typical price rose and out when it fell. It takes no series and needs volume.

functions.name: obv
functions.text: On-balance volume: a running total that adds a bar’s volume when the close rose and takes it off when it fell, starting at 0 on the first bar. It takes no series and needs volume.

functions.name: vwap
functions.summary: volume-weighted average price of the last n bars
functions.text: Volume-weighted average of the typical price (high + low + close) / 3 over the last n bars. It takes no series and needs volume.

functions.name: keltner_upper
functions.text: Upper Keltner channel: the n-bar exponential average plus width times the average true range over atr bars, which is read from the ticker’s own bars. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in keltner_upper(volume, 20, 2, 10).

functions.name: keltner_lower
functions.text: Lower Keltner channel: the n-bar exponential average minus width times the average true range over atr bars, which is read from the ticker’s own bars. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in keltner_lower(volume, 20, 2, 10).

functions.name: supertrend
functions.summary: supertrend line, under the price in an uptrend
functions.text: Supertrend line: bands at (high + low) / 2 plus and minus mult average true ranges over n bars, each moving only towards the price until the close crosses it, the lower band in an uptrend and the upper in a downtrend. It takes no series.

functions.name: supertrend_up
functions.summary: condition: the supertrend is in an uptrend
functions.text: A condition that is true while the supertrend is in an uptrend, with its line under the price, and false in a downtrend. It takes no series.

functions.name: wma
functions.summary: weighted average of the last n values
functions.text: Linearly weighted average of the last n values, the newest weighing n and the oldest 1. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in wma(volume, 20).

functions.name: hma
functions.text: Hull moving average: the weighted average over sqrt(n) bars of twice the weighted average over n / 2 bars minus the one over n bars, with n / 2 and sqrt(n) rounded down. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in hma(volume, 20).

functions.name: median
functions.summary: median of the last n values
functions.text: Median of the last n values, the mean of the two middle ones when n is even. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in median(volume, 20).

functions.name: zscore
functions.summary: standard deviations from the n-bar average
functions.text: How many standard deviations the value is from its average over the last n values, dividing by n as stdev does, and unknown when they are all equal. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in zscore(volume, 20).

functions.name: percent_rank
functions.summary: share of the previous n values below this one
functions.text: The share of the previous n values that are below this one, from 0 to 100. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in percent_rank(volume, 20).

functions.name: slope
functions.summary: least-squares slope over n bars, per bar
functions.text: Slope of the least-squares line through the last n values, in the series’ units per bar. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in slope(volume, 20).

functions.name: correl
functions.text: Correlation, from -1 to 1, of the one-bar changes of this ticker’s close and of the series written first, over the last n bars, unknown when either one is constant. It reads close for this ticker; the series written first is read as of reads it, so it lines up with this ticker’s bars.

functions.name: count
functions.summary: how many of the last n bars a condition held
functions.text: How many of the last n bars the condition held, this one included, and unknown while any of them is unknown. It takes no series, only a condition.

functions.name: bars_since
functions.summary: bars since a condition was last true
functions.text: Bars since the condition was last true: 0 on a bar where it is, and unknown until it has been true. It takes no series, only a condition.
functions.example: buy when bars_since(close crosses above sma(50)) < 10

functions.name: sum
functions.summary: sum of the last n values
functions.text: Sum of the last n values. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in sum(volume, 20).

functions.name: dema
functions.summary: double exponential average, less lag than ema
functions.text: Double exponential average, 2 * e1 - e2 with e1 = ema(n) and e2 the ema of e1 over n bars, which follows the price with less lag than ema. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in dema(volume, 20).

functions.name: tema
functions.summary: triple exponential average, less lag than ema
functions.text: Triple exponential average, 3 * e1 - 3 * e2 + e3 with e1 = ema(n) and each next one the ema of the one before, which follows the price with less lag than dema. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in tema(volume, 20).

functions.name: kama
functions.text: Kaufman’s adaptive average, which follows the price closely while it runs and slowly while it chops: each bar it moves the share sc = (ER * (2 / (fast + 1) - 2 / (slow + 1)) + 2 / (slow + 1)) squared of the way to the price, ER being the efficiency ratio over n bars, and it starts from the price of the bar before the first bar where ER is known. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in kama(volume, 10, 2, 30).

functions.name: aroon_up
functions.summary: aroon up, 0 to 100: how recent the high is
functions.text: Aroon up, from 0 to 100: 100 * (n - bars since the highest high of the last n + 1 bars) / n, so 100 on a bar that makes the high and 0 when it was n bars ago, a tie going to the most recent bar. It takes no series and reads the ticker’s own highs.

functions.name: aroon_down
functions.summary: aroon down, 0 to 100: how recent the low is
functions.text: Aroon down, from 0 to 100: 100 * (n - bars since the lowest low of the last n + 1 bars) / n, so 100 on a bar that makes the low and 0 when it was n bars ago, a tie going to the most recent bar. It takes no series and reads the ticker’s own lows.

functions.name: psar
functions.summary: parabolic SAR, a stop that trails the price
functions.text: Wilder’s parabolic SAR, a stop that trails the price, under the lows in an uptrend and over the highs in a downtrend: its pace starts at step, grows by step with each new extreme and stops at max, a bar that crosses it reverses the trend, and the first trend is up when the second close is above the first. It takes no series, and step may not be above max.
functions.example: buy when close crosses above psar()

functions.name: cmf
functions.text: Chaikin money flow, from -1 to 1: the sum over the last n bars of ((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) * volume, over the sum of their volume, a bar with no range adding 0. It takes no series and needs volume.

functions.name: linreg
functions.text: The value at this bar of the least-squares straight line through the last n values, against the bar number, whose slope per bar is slope(n). Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in linreg(volume, 20).

functions.name: rsquared
functions.summary: how well a line fits the last n values, 0 to 1
functions.text: How well the least-squares straight line through the last n values fits them, from 0 to 1 (1 when they lie on a line), and unknown when they are all equal. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in rsquared(volume, 20).

functions.name: efficiency
functions.text: Kaufman’s efficiency ratio, from 0 to 1: how far the value moved over n bars, |x - x[n]|, over how far it travelled, the sum of |x - x[1]| over those bars, so 1 is a straight run, and unknown when it did not move. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in efficiency(volume, 20).
functions.example: buy when efficiency(20) > 0.3 and close > sma(50)

functions.name: streak
functions.summary: bars in a row up (1, 2, ...) or down (-1, -2, ...)
functions.text: Consecutive bars the value rose (1, 2, 3, ...) or fell (-1, -2, ...), 0 on a bar equal to the one before, and unknown on the first bar and where a value is unknown, counting again from the next known change. Without a series it reads close; write another first, as in streak(volume).

functions.name: min
functions.text: The smaller of two values.

functions.name: max
functions.text: The larger of two values.

functions.name: abs
functions.text: The value without its sign.

functions.name: sqrt
functions.text: The square root of the value, unknown below 0.

functions.name: log
functions.text: The natural logarithm of the value, unknown at 0 and below.

functions.name: exp
functions.text: e raised to the power of the value, unknown when too large to hold.

functions.name: if
functions.summary: a where the condition holds, otherwise b
functions.text: The number a where the condition holds and b where it does not, and unknown where the condition is unknown; a and b are numbers, not conditions.

functions.name: column
functions.summary: a column of a CSV file: column(score) of signals
functions.text: Reads a numeric column of a CSV file by its header, in lower case with underscores for spaces, such as column(score) of signals. A row counts as known at the close of the day it is dated.

series.name: open
series.text: The open price of each bar of the ticker the rule belongs to. With Yahoo data prices are adjusted for splits and dividends, so compare them with an average, not a fixed number.

series.name: high
series.text: The highest price of each bar of the ticker the rule belongs to. With Yahoo data prices are adjusted for splits and dividends, so compare them with an average, not a fixed number.

series.name: low
series.text: The lowest price of each bar of the ticker the rule belongs to. With Yahoo data prices are adjusted for splits and dividends, so compare them with an average, not a fixed number.

series.name: close
series.text: The close price of each bar of the ticker the rule belongs to. With Yahoo data prices are adjusted for splits and dividends, so compare them with an average, not a fixed number.

series.name: volume
series.text: The traded volume of each bar of the ticker the rule belongs to.

calendar.name: month
calendar.text: The month of the bar, 1 to 12. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: day
calendar.text: The day of the month, 1 to 31. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: weekday
calendar.text: The day of the week: 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: year
calendar.text: The year, such as 2024. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: month_start
calendar.text: A condition: the first bar of a month. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: month_end
calendar.text: A condition: the last bar of a month. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: quarter
calendar.text: The quarter of the year of the bar, 1 to 4. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: week_start
calendar.text: A condition: the first bar of a week, which starts on Monday. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: week_end
calendar.text: A condition: the last bar of a week, which starts on Monday. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: quarter_start
calendar.text: A condition: the first bar of a quarter. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: quarter_end
calendar.text: A condition: the last bar of a quarter. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: year_start
calendar.text: A condition: the first bar of a year. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: year_end
calendar.text: A condition: the last bar of a year. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: trading_day
calendar.summary: number of the day in its month, counting days with a bar
calendar.text: The number of the bar’s day within its month, counting the days that have a bar: 1 on the month’s first such day, the same for every bar of a day, and unknown in the data’s first month, which may have begun before it. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

calendar.name: trading_days_left
calendar.summary: days with a bar left in the month
calendar.text: The days with a bar left in the month after the bar’s day, 0 on the month’s last such day, counting past the last bar the days it would go on to have, so a holiday it does not know of is counted. It is read from each bar’s date in UTC.

position.name: bars held
position.summary: completed bars since the entry filled, 0 on that bar
position.text: The number of completed bars since the buy filled (for a short, the short sale), or with several entries the first; it is 0 on the bar of the fill. Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not inside a function, over a window of bars, with [n] or with of.

position.name: entry price
position.summary: the price the position was bought or sold short at
position.text: The price the position was bought at, slippage included, or for a short the price it was sold at; with several entries, their average price. Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not inside a function, over a window of bars, with [n] or with of.

position.name: last entry price
position.summary: the price of the latest entry
position.text: The price the latest entry of the position filled at, slippage included; with one entry it is the entry price. Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not inside a function, over a window of bars, with [n] or with of.
position.example: sell when close < last entry price * 0.95

position.name: entries made
position.summary: how many entries the position has
position.text: How many entries the open position has made: 1 after the buy or short sale, then one more for each add. Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not inside a function, over a window of bars, with [n] or with of.
position.example: sell when entries made == 1 and bars held >= 10

position.name: highest since entry
position.summary: the highest price since the position was entered
position.text: The highest price since the position's first entry: its fill price before slippage, then the high of each later bar, and of the fill bar too when it filled at that bar's open. Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not inside a function, over a window of bars, with [n] or with of.
position.example: sell when close < highest since entry - 3 * atr(22)

position.name: lowest since entry
position.summary: the lowest price since the position was entered
position.text: The lowest price since the position's first entry: its fill price before slippage, then the low of each later bar, and of the fill bar too when it filled at that bar's open. Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not inside a function, over a window of bars, with [n] or with of.
position.example:
short when close < sma(200)
cover when close > lowest since entry + 3 * atr(22)

position.name: position return
position.summary: the open position’s return at this close, before costs
position.text: The open position's return at this close before costs: close / entry price - 1 for a long, 1 - close / entry price for a short. Only sell, cover and add rules can read it, and not inside a function, over a window of bars, with [n] or with of.
position.example: sell when position return > 20% or bars held > 30

settings.name: name
settings.summary: title shown above the result
settings.text: The title shown above the result. Without it the title is Backtest.

settings.name: universe
settings.summary: tickers and weights: SPY 60%, TLT 40%
settings.text: The tickers to trade, each with an optional weight: give every ticker one, or none. Weights add up to at most 200%: what is left under 100% stays in cash, and above 100% the strategy borrows.

settings.name: symbol
settings.summary: one ticker (same as universe)
settings.text: Another way to write universe.

settings.name: from
settings.summary: first day, as 2015-01-31
settings.text: The first day of the run. Without it the run starts on the first day every ticker has prices.

settings.name: to
settings.summary: last day, as 2024-12-31
settings.text: The last day of the run, whole day included, and it must come after from. Without it the run ends on the last day with prices.

settings.name: data
settings.summary: where plain tickers come from: yahoo, binance or tiingo
settings.text: Where tickers written without a prefix come from, the plugin setting deciding without it, though a plain ticker that starts with ^, such as ^VIX or ^IRX, comes from Yahoo whatever data says. yahoo:, binance:, tiingo:, fred: or csv: in front of a ticker picks that ticker’s own source.

values.summary: Yahoo prices, adjusted for splits and dividends
values.text: Plain tickers come from Yahoo, spelt the way Yahoo spells them, such as SPY, BRK-B, BTC-USD or ^GSPC. Yahoo gives 1d and 1w bars.

values.summary: Binance market symbols, such as BTCUSDT
values.text: Plain tickers are Binance market symbols, such as BTCUSDT, though one that starts with ^, such as ^VIX, still comes from Yahoo. Binance gives bars from 1m up to 1w.

values.summary: Tiingo prices, adjusted for splits and dividends
values.text: Plain tickers come from Tiingo, with the key chosen under Tiingo API key in the plugin settings, though one that starts with ^, such as ^VIX or the cash rate ^IRX, still comes from Yahoo, which alone has them. Tiingo gives 1d and 1w bars of US stocks, ETFs and funds.

settings.name: interval
settings.summary: bar size: 1d, 1w, or 1h and others on Binance
settings.text: The bar size, 1d unless you say otherwise. Yahoo and Tiingo give 1d and 1w, Binance gives 1m up to 1w, and one interval applies to every ticker.

values.text: 1-minute bars. Only Binance gives them, so the block needs data: binance or a binance: ticker.
3-minute bars. Only Binance gives them, so the block needs data: binance or a binance: ticker.
5-minute bars. Only Binance gives them, so the block needs data: binance or a binance: ticker.
15-minute bars. Only Binance gives them, so the block needs data: binance or a binance: ticker.
30-minute bars. Only Binance gives them, so the block needs data: binance or a binance: ticker.
1-hour bars. Only Binance gives them, so the block needs data: binance or a binance: ticker.
2-hour bars. Only Binance gives them, so the block needs data: binance or a binance: ticker.
4-hour bars. Only Binance gives them, so the block needs data: binance or a binance: ticker.
6-hour bars. Only Binance gives them, so the block needs data: binance or a binance: ticker.
8-hour bars. Only Binance gives them, so the block needs data: binance or a binance: ticker.
12-hour bars. Only Binance gives them, so the block needs data: binance or a binance: ticker.
Daily bars, from Yahoo, Tiingo or Binance.
3-day bars. Only Binance gives them, so the block needs data: binance or a binance: ticker.
Weekly bars, from Yahoo, Tiingo or Binance. A weekly bar is used once its week is over.

settings.name: capital
settings.summary: starting money, as 10000 or 10k
settings.text: The starting money, written 10000 or 10k (m is millions). Without it the plugin’s Starting money setting is used.

settings.name: costs
settings.summary: per trade, as 5 bps or 0.05%
settings.text: The cost of each trade, written 5 bps or 0.05%. A plain number counts as bps, and the cost must be under 10%.

settings.name: slippage
settings.summary: how much worse each fill is than the price, as 5 bps
settings.text: How much worse each fill is than the price: a buy or a cover fills higher, and a sell or a short sale lower. It is written like costs.

settings.name: size
settings.summary: share of equity to use when tickers have no weights
settings.text: The share of equity to use when the tickers have no weights, up to 200%, borrowing above 100%. You cannot give weights and size together.

settings.name: rebalance
settings.signature: rebalance: never | weekly | monthly | quarterly | yearly
settings.summary: never, weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly
settings.text: How often held tickers go back to their weights. Without it, never.

values.summary: positions are never put back to their weights
values.text: Held positions are never put back to their weights. This is the default.

values.summary: back to the weights at the start of each week
values.text: Each held ticker goes back to its target weight at the open of its first bar in each new week. Weeks start on Monday.

values.summary: back to the weights at the start of each month
values.text: Each held ticker goes back to its target weight at the open of its first bar in each new month. A rebalance never opens a position.

values.summary: back to the weights at the start of each quarter
values.text: Each held ticker goes back to its target weight at the open of its first bar in each new quarter. A rebalance never opens a position.

values.summary: back to the weights at the start of each year
values.text: Each held ticker goes back to its target weight at the open of its first bar in each new year. A rebalance never opens a position.

settings.name: benchmark
settings.summary: ticker to compare with, bought and held
settings.text: The ticker to compare the result with, bought and held. Without it the benchmark is your own tickers at their weights.

settings.name: stop loss
settings.summary: sell this far below the entry price (above it for a short), as 10% or 2 atr(14)
settings.text: Sells when the price falls this far below the entry price, or buys a short back when it rises this far above it, as a percentage or as a number of average true ranges. A percentage must be above 0% and at most 99%.

settings.name: trailing stop
settings.summary: sell this far below the highest price since entry (above the lowest for a short)
settings.text: Sells when the price falls this far below the highest price since entry, or buys a short back when it rises this far above the lowest. A percentage must be above 0% and at most 99%.

settings.name: take profit
settings.summary: sell this far above the entry price (below it for a short)
settings.text: Sells when the price rises this far above the entry price, or buys a short back when it falls this far below it. A percentage must be above 0% and at most 1000%, and a short can never reach one of 100% or more.

settings.name: cash rate
settings.summary: what cash earns: 4% a year, or a yield ticker such as ^IRX
settings.text: What cash earns a year, written 4%, or a ticker whose close is a yearly yield, such as ^IRX or fred:DGS3MO. A rate needs its percent sign and must be at most 50%.

settings.name: borrow fee
settings.summary: yearly fee on the value of short positions, 0.5% unless set
settings.text: A yearly fee on the value of each short position at the close, paid for every day it is held and counted in the trade’s return. Without it the plugin’s Borrow fee for shorts setting is used, 0.5% at first, and it must be between 0% and 100%.

settings.name: margin rate
settings.summary: yearly interest on money borrowed, 6% unless set
settings.text: Yearly interest on money borrowed, paid between two bars when cash less the value of the shorts is below 0, as it is when the strategy holds more than its equity. Without it the plugin’s Interest on borrowed money setting is used, 6% at first, and it must be between 0% and 50%.

settings.name: test from
settings.summary: report results before and from this day apart
settings.text: Reports the results before this day and from it apart. It is one run split in two with nothing re-fitted, and the day must lie after from and before to.

settings.name: hold
settings.summary: hold only the best-ranked tickers: top 3 by roc(126)
settings.text: Holds only the tickers with the highest score, such as the top 3 by roc(126). The score is a number written like a value in a rule, and the universe takes no weights.

settings.name: weighting
settings.summary: inverse volatility(60): calmer tickers get more weight
settings.text: Calmer tickers get more weight: each share is in proportion to 1 divided by the volatility over the last n one-bar returns. The period must be at least 2.

settings.name: risk per trade
settings.summary: size each buy or short sale by what it risks: 1% at 2 atr(14)
settings.text: Sizes each buy so that a fall of that many average true ranges loses that share of equity, and each short sale so that a rise does, up to the ticker’s weight. It cannot be used with weighting, or with a rebalance other than never.

settings.name: fill
settings.summary: when rules fill: at the next open, or at the same close
settings.text: When a rule fills. With next open, the default, a rule read at a bar’s close fills at the next open; with close it fills at that same close.

values.summary: a rule read at a close fills at the next open
values.text: A rule read at a bar’s close fills at that ticker’s next open. This is the default.

values.summary: a rule read at a close fills at that same close
values.text: A rule read at a bar’s close fills at that same close.

settings.name: commission
settings.summary: charge per order: 1, or 0.005 per share, min 1, max 1%
settings.text: A charge on every order in the account’s money, added to costs: a fixed amount per order, or an amount per share with an optional minimum and a cap as a share of the order’s value. Without it the plugin setting applies, which is none at first.

settings.name: entries
settings.summary: build each position in up to 3 entries, each a third
settings.text: Builds each position in up to that many entries, each a step of its whole size: the buy rule makes the first and the add rule each later one. It needs an add rule, and the entries together never go above the ticker’s weight.
settings.example:
entries: 3
add when close > last entry price * 1.03

settings.name: magnify
settings.summary: look inside each bar with 1h bars, for stops and targets
settings.text: Follows a bar that holds a stop or target through smaller bars inside it, such as 1h bars inside daily ones, so the order in which the stop and the target are reached is read, not assumed. Rules stay on the strategy’s own bars, and Yahoo gives 2m to 1h bars inside daily bars for recent days only and 1d bars inside weekly ones.

words.name: between
words.summary: inside a range, both ends included
words.text: True when a is at least lo and at most hi, so rsi(2) between 10 and 30 means rsi(2) >= 10 and rsi(2) <= 30. It does not chain, and it is read as one comparison, so not rsi(2) between 10 and 30 holds outside the range.

words.name: for … bars
words.summary: held on each of the last n bars
words.text: True when the condition held on each of the last n bars, this one included, and unknown until all n are known. It applies to the comparison before it and a not in front of it, so a and b for 3 bars means a and (b for 3 bars), and not up for 3 bars means (not up) for 3 bars: use brackets for more.
words.example: buy when close > sma(200) for 3 bars

words.name: within
words.summary: held on at least one of the last n bars
words.text: True when the condition held on at least one of the last n bars, this one included, and unknown until all n are known. n is a whole number from 1 to 10000 or a parameter, and bar is also accepted.

words.name: buy when
words.summary: condition that opens a long position
words.text: Opens a long position in a ticker you do not hold when the condition is true at a close. It fills at that ticker’s next open, unless the fill setting says close.

words.name: sell when
words.summary: condition that closes a long position
words.text: Closes a long position when the condition is true at a close. Without a sell rule a position is held until a stop or a short rule closes it, or the run ends.

words.name: add when
words.summary: condition that adds the next entry
words.text: Adds the next entry to the position held, long or short, when the condition is true at a close, until the entries setting’s count is made. It needs an entries line, and it is skipped at a close where the sell rule, or for a short the cover rule, holds.
words.example:
entries: 3
add when close > last entry price * 1.03

words.name: short when
words.summary: condition that opens a short position
words.text: Sells short a ticker you do not hold when the condition is true at a close, so the position gains as the price falls; it fills as a buy would. A ticker held long is closed by it, and turns short at the same fill when the buy rule does not hold there too.

words.name: cover when
words.summary: condition that closes a short position
words.text: Buys a short position back when the condition is true at a close; it needs a short rule. Without a cover rule a short is held until a stop or the buy rule closes it, or the run ends.
words.example:
short when close < sma(200)
cover when close > sma(200)

words.name: for
words.summary: rules and stops for one ticker or several: for TLT:
words.text: Starts rules for one ticker, or for several separated by commas, as in for SPY, TLT:; each must be in the universe. A buy, sell, short, cover or add rule, stop loss, trailing stop or take profit written below it replaces the shared one for those tickers only.

words.name: for all
words.summary: back to the rules every ticker shares
words.text: Goes back to the rules every ticker shares. What you write after it applies to every ticker that has no rule of its own.

words.name: and
words.summary: both conditions hold
words.text: True when both conditions are true. A rule can continue on the next line: indent it and start it with and or or.
words.example: buy when close > sma(200) and rsi(14) < 70

words.name: or
words.summary: either condition holds
words.text: True when either condition is true. It binds loosest, so a and b or c reads as (a and b) or c.
words.example: sell when close < sma(200) or rsi(14) > 85

words.name: not
words.summary: the condition does not hold
words.text: True when the condition after it is not true. It binds tighter than and but looser than a comparison, so not close > 1 reads as not (close > 1), and a window after it covers it: not up for 3 bars is (not up) for 3 bars.

words.name: crosses
words.summary: changed sides: crossed above or below
words.text: True on a bar where a crosses above or below b: it is on the other side of b than it was on the previous bar. Write crosses above or crosses below for one direction only.

words.name: crosses above
words.summary: was at or below, is now above
words.text: True on a bar where a is above b and was at or below b on the previous bar.
words.example: buy when sma(50) crosses above sma(200)

words.name: crosses below
words.summary: was at or above, is now below
words.text: True on a bar where a is below b and was at or above b on the previous bar.
words.example: sell when sma(50) crosses below sma(200)

words.name: above
words.summary: same as >
words.text: The same as >. You can also write is above.

words.name: below
words.summary: same as <
words.text: The same as <. You can also write is below.

words.name: of
words.summary: another ticker's value: sma(200) of SPY
words.text: Reads a value from another ticker, which does not have to be in the universe. For each bar you get that ticker’s latest bar that had ended by the time this bar ended.
words.example: buy when close > sma(200) and close of ^VIX < 25

words.name: tiingo:
words.summary: a ticker from Tiingo, such as tiingo:SPY
words.text: Takes this ticker’s daily prices from Tiingo, adjusted for splits and dividends, with the key chosen under Tiingo API key in the plugin settings. Tiingo gives 1d and 1w bars of US stocks, ETFs and funds.

words.name: fred:
words.summary: an economic series from FRED, such as fred:T10Y2Y
words.text: A series from FRED, each value counted from the day it was first published, with the key chosen under FRED API key in the plugin settings. Rules read it with of, as in close of fred:T10Y2Y, and cash rate takes a yield such as fred:DGS3MO, but it cannot be traded or be the benchmark.

words.name: [n]
words.summary: the value n bars earlier: close[5]
words.text: The value n bars earlier, so close[5] is the close five bars back. It works on any value, and n must be a whole number or a parameter that is one.

words.name: in … step
words.summary: a range to try: 50 in 20..100 step 10
words.text: Gives a parameter a range of values worth trying; the block still runs with the value before in, which must lie inside the range. The step is optional and is 1 unless you write it, or 1% for a percentage.

words.name: top … by
words.summary: hold the 3 tickers with the highest score
words.text: Inside hold: how many tickers to hold, and the score that ranks them, written like a value in a rule. The universe must have at least that many tickers.

words.name: at
words.summary: share of equity risked at a stop distance
words.text: Inside risk per trade: it joins the share of equity at risk to the distance, in average true ranges, that the price is assumed to move against the position.

words.name: true
words.summary: always holds
words.text: A condition that always holds. always means the same.

words.name: false
words.summary: never holds
words.text: A condition that never holds. never means the same.

units.text: A percentage. It counts as the number 0.05 wherever a number is expected, so roc(20) > 5% means roc(20) > 0.05.

units.name: bps
units.text: Basis points: hundredths of a percent, so 100 bps is 1%. In costs and slippage a plain number counts as bps too.

laterWords.about: Words added after 0.7.0. A block may still use one as a parameter or definition name, which it then means in that block; calling it as a function there is an error.
